cases.description: Exact context can put a less frequent local action ahead of a more frequent action learned in another resource kind.
Changing the resource context selects the habit learned there.
Synthetic Ex and picker surface facts give direct commits the same ranking credit.
Swapping synthetic surface labels leaves the same frontier order.
One local use outweighs three uses in each of two other projects because only the strongest other project contributes.
Current-session heat can lift an earlier equal-use choice above a more recent choice from another session.
Without current-session heat, equal-score choices use event recency.
One newer use does not outweigh five direct uses only one active day old.
Twenty-one later active days remove old score even though the calendar gap itself is not a penalty.
A dispatch exactly 365 calendar days old still contributes after an idle gap.
A dispatch older than 365 calendar days contributes no score even without intervening activity.
A single direct dispatch does not meet the default promotion threshold.
Two direct executions promote a valid path while they are within five active days.
A promotion disappears once its direct executions are five active days old.
Repeated ordinary-slot invocations promote the stable slot-position identity.
A previously promoted shortcut remains eligible after original direct events leave the 365-day horizon; a recently repeated path ranks above it.
Accepting a nested choice replaces the whole token at the cursor and preserves following spacing and text.
Accepting a root replaces the complete token without changing the following arguments.
A command separator ends the token; accepting preserves the following command.
Accepting a note value replaces only the typed slot token, preserving the following text.
Cursor positions are byte offsets and a multibyte suffix within the token is replaced completely.
A learned choice remains scored at active-day age 20, the last day inside a 21-day window.
The same choice has zero score at active-day age 21 and the structural order returns.
The calendar cutoff uses the offset on the earlier local date, rather than a fixed 365-day duration.
A cutoff at a nonexistent local time advances by the spring clock gap.
A cutoff at a repeated local time selects standard time.
For equal timestamps, writer ID, not fixture array order, determines the later credited event.
For equal timestamps and writer, log position determines the later credited event.
Equal-time events from one writer keep log-position order after later events and a backward clock movement.
Direct and shortcut commits on the same surface remain distinct; shortcuts cannot add promotion credit and overtake a stronger path.
When direct history has expired, later shortcut use does not break a zero-score promotion tie; rendered path does.
A host-declared node ID can differ from its token spelling.
More uses of Alpha rank Alpha ahead of Beta among indexed candidates.
Changing only the resource usage history changes the indexed candidate order.
Host match quality is added to the resource usage score and can change the candidate order.
A resource selected after a promoted shortcut receives its own usage credit without adding path credit.
Resource usage in the exact Lua context can outrank more uses in Python.
The same resource events rank the Python habit first in the Python context.
The same resource ID used under a different slot cannot change this slot’s resource ranking.
A declared rename fact transfers earlier resource usage to the current ID without adding use.
Identical sequences in the same project with different contexts, and different projects with the same context, retain separate support and scores.
Sequences with the same capability IDs but different complete step arguments remain separate groups.
Accepting a namespace advances without dispatching.
Committing a terminal choice dispatches it.
A hybrid can explicitly advance without dispatching.
A hybrid can explicitly commit its own action.
Equal-score equal-time tie follows logical writer order even when the current writer sorts first.
A repeated half-hour wall time uses the later occurrence for the 365-day cutoff.
A native command retains its root and argument-presence fact for replay.
The recorded path credits an existing ancestor after its executed descendant is removed.
A stable node ID retains its usage across an actual token rename between recording and replay.
A typed prefix ranks its leading matching block; a nonmatch separates a later match from that block.
Ordinary suggestions share slot-position score and retain provider order even when values would sort differently.
A nonmatching indexed candidate is excluded even with the strongest usage and the same zero match quality.
Unused resources with equal match quality follow index position, not their IDs.
One invocation records and credits its source and destination resource IDs independently.
The same invocations also credit the destination slot for each committed selection.
Resource selections through a shortcut do not give that path credit that could overtake another promotion.
A rename fact does not add a use or recency that would outrank a later equally used resource.
A rename alone does not advance the project to active-day age 21 and erase the last resource score, which would let Beta match quality win.
The 51-day flow cutoff retains events at or after the same earlier local wall time.
The same flow events expire later on the cutoff date when they are older than the wall-time cutoff.
Equal flow scores use descending support before recency.
Tied promotions compare rendered paths by ascending UTF-8 bytes, putting zebra before éclair.
Selecting a resource records its ID in navigation state without committing.
A missing required resource prevents commit.
A complete resource choice commits the selected slot-to-resource mapping.
Backtracking leaves the resource slot and clears its selection without committing.
An empty optional resource slot does not block a commit or create a selected resource.
A moved node keeps its own credit under the same stable ID.
A moved node needs current-writer heat to outrank a competitor with stronger durable evidence.
A moved node leaves historical edge and ancestor credit at its old parent.
A move does not credit the new parent edge for historical uses.
A token rename preserves promotion evidence for an unchanged stable-ID path.
A different node reusing the old spelling does not inherit a moved path promotion.
A resource rename does not change structural choices or competing promotions.
Flow replay resolves a stable moved node through its current capability.
Flow lookback uses the later occurrence of a repeated Lord Howe wall time, retaining the cutoff itself.
Flow lookback uses the later occurrence of a repeated Lord Howe wall time, retaining the cutoff itself.
A native event breaks a flow sequence.
A semantic event with arguments breaks a flow sequence.
Current-writer semantic events persist argument presence and break flow sequences.
Clearing argument presence makes the same complete capability steps eligible for proposals.
Equal score, support and recency sort by IDs derived from the complete group key.
Entering an ordinary value retains its transient ID and advances to the resource slot without dispatch.
Mixed ordinary and resource navigation preserves transient input without recording its value.
Mixed ordinary and resource navigation preserves transient input without recording its value.
Mixed ordinary and resource navigation preserves transient input without recording its value.
Uses on both sides of a move retain node credit and their own historical edges.
Resource ranking uses recorded IDs across an index-label change and does not need the recording inventory.
Typing an unambiguous resource label commits its ID and slot target without storing the text.
An unresolved or ambiguous typed resource remains uncommitted.
An unresolved or ambiguous typed resource remains uncommitted.
An omitted optional slot is absent from the event before a filled resource slot.
The ID resolved from typed commit receives resource credit and outranks index order.
A multi-slot commit credits the last filled slot as target and propagates to the action.
Two multi-slot commits promote the complete slot-position identity while rendering to the first slot.
A path can omit an optional slot and retain the later filled slot as its target.
Context components are composed within each other project before taking the strongest project.
Typing a root prefix suppresses otherwise eligible ordinary promotions.
Seven qualifying project groups are sorted before the default limit of six.
One event supplying two capability steps counts as one occurrence without splitting its steps.
Typing a resource after an ordinary slot commits only one resolved ID.
Typing a resource after an ordinary slot commits only one resolved ID.
Typing a resource after an ordinary slot commits only one resolved ID.
The ID from a typed mixed-slot commit receives resource credit ahead of index order.
Equal strongest-project scores use their latest credited event.
A later event in a weaker project can break the strongest-score tie.
Resource rename facts do not interrupt the invocation stream.
A command from another project interrupts the sequence.
The same two-step action does not yield proposals when the host identifies it as an existing flow.
512 intervening non-invocation facts do not evict supported invocation history.
A native shortcut retains origin and does not receive direct node credit.
